reasons: The cited clause has automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanic; the only exit from a renewal is a 90-day convenience termination, so the effective opt-out window (90 days) fails the fallback (≤60 days) — deviation classification is correct and not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

The redline is the minimal effective fix: it inserts a Customer 30-day non-renewal right into the automatic-renewal sentence, reaching the preferred position, and leaves the mutual 90-day convenience-termination right (which also benefits us) intact. The 12-month renewal term already complies.

Correctly declines to force a price-uplift cap where fees are a revenue share set per Exhibit, and notes the absent vendor renewal reminder in the rationale rather than flagging it separately — consistent with playbook handling of minor sub-elements.

The failed deterministic check (value=90) reflects the retained convenience-termination sentence, not a defect in the edit; the inserted 30-day non-renewal notice governs exit from renewal. Minor residual drafting risk (the 'Neither Party may terminate during the Initial Term' sentence could be read against a late-Initial-Term non-renewal notice) is cosmetic and could be cured with a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' lead-in.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states what changed and why, and offers the 60-day fallback.
